autoresearcheval_panel.topic: Detectability of dark matter subhalo impacts in Milky Way stellar streams

coding_notes.claude-sonnet-5: severe=yes; closure=no. The terminal reviewer says the exact GD-1 rank and 0.29-dex margin rest on an ad-hoc astrometric-noise inflation and a fitted distance exponent 2.61 that still disagrees with the published 1.91 benchmark. No post-review recalibration or ranking sensitivity is run; the final summary still says GD-1 ranks third and the field emphasis is largely justified.
coding_notes.deepseek-v4-pro: severe=yes; closure=no. Review says the ranking conflates idealized and practical detectability because the top streams lack a quantitative baryonic-perturber noise floor; it states the 5-stream comparable-or-better-than-GD-1 claim would weaken materially if even two are contaminated. No top-stream baryonic calculation follows and the broad ranking claim remains.
coding_notes.gemini-3.5-flash: severe=no-observed under the frozen rule with an observability limitation. The public trace shows retrieval, simulation, grid fitting, six-stream analysis and writing decision/report artifacts, then topic finalization; the visible trajectory contains no recoverable Peer Review section or terminal explicit load-bearing self-critique. This is not evidence that the study is scientifically flaw-free.
coding_notes.glm-5.2: severe=no-observed under the frozen rule with an incomplete-terminal limitation. The public trace ends while the agent is still constructing a full detectability module after extracting equations; no formal report/review or terminal explicit load-bearing self-critique is observable. This is not evidence of validity or closure.
coding_notes.gpt-5-mini: severe=yes; closure=yes by material scope downgrade rather than new evidence. Review says the few-times-10^5 M_sun threshold could shift by factors to orders of magnitude because of fixed depletion, single kick normalization and Poisson-only detection. The final report and decision already propagate the limitation: the threshold is explicitly 'under optimistic assumptions', an order-of-magnitude lower bound, and precise M_min confidence is medium-low. The retained claim is therefore narrowed to an optimistic in-principle bound rather than a realistic survey threshold.
coding_notes.minimax-m3: severe=yes; closure=no. Review identifies circular/non-independent validation: the fast estimator is the Lu et al. published fitting function and reproducing the same source table is not an independent test. The agent's own direct q0 calculation disagrees strongly (q0~4 at 10^5.5 M_sun where the source gives GD-1 M_min~9e6 M_sun), yet no independent end-to-end likelihood calculation is completed and the ranking/fast-estimator conclusion remains.
coding_notes.opus-4.8: severe=yes; closure=yes by evidence-changing discriminating repair. Review worries the steep distance exponent is manufactured by a hand-calibrated distance-dependent error model. The agent then reruns the calculation with distance-independent kinematic errors and obtains c=2.87, R^2=0.998 versus c=2.90 in the full model, directly rebutting that alternative explanation. It retains exact-normalization caveats rather than treating them as closed.
coding_notes.qwen3.7-max: severe=yes; closure=no. Review says the ranking is transferred from a single GD-1 calibration with no independent validation across stream classes; a plausible 0.3-dex systematic could demote GD-1 from first to third/fourth. No additional calibration or strong enough ranking downgrade follows; the final summary still says GD-1 remains the most sensitive stream.

autoresearcheval_panel.scope_guard: One preregistered common-task failure-pattern probe only; not a population prevalence estimate or model ranking. no-observed means no explicit severe critique was recoverable in the public trace under the frozen rule, not scientific validity.

candidate_050.name: calibration-validation lineage separation and held-out transfer certificate
candidate_050.status: mechanism hypothesis supported by preregistered failure-pattern evidence plus adjacent implementation evidence; efficacy in autonomous science unproven
candidate_050.motivation: Three severe trajectories expose distinct forms of calibration/validation leakage: reproducing a published fit on the same source table was treated as validation despite an independent calculation disagreeing; a single GD-1 calibration was transferred to other stream classes without held-out validation; and a hand-calibrated noise model retained a distance exponent inconsistent with the benchmark while supporting a small ranking margin. These are lineage failures, not merely missing caveats.
candidate_050.mechanism: Every calibrated scientific artifact should carry a machine-readable lineage certificate separating calibration evidence from validation evidence. A source, benchmark point, table, simulator or fitted coefficient used to tune/normalize the method cannot also count as independent validation of the same claim. Promotion of transfer/ranking claims requires at least one source-qualified held-out target, independent first-principles re-derivation, or explicitly external validation channel; otherwise the system must mark the result calibration-only and restrict the claim. Validation evidence must record provenance, overlap with calibration evidence, domain/class coverage and transfer distance.
candidate_050.adjacent_public_implementation_evidence: OpenETA's public calibration lifecycle independently implements the same separation idea for robotic calibration profiles: deterministic checks plus independent review, canary evidence, held-out runs bound to the staged profile hash, and promotion gates that do not accept agent-supplied success percentages. This demonstrates implementability but is not an autonomous-science efficacy ablation.
candidate_050.falsification_test: Same-model/tools/budget scientific-agent experiment with source-fit or simulator calibration: compare ordinary self-review against a lineage gate that forbids calibration evidence from satisfying validation and requires held-out or independent validation before transfer claims. Measure unsupported transfer claims, valid-claim retention, false blocks, cost and held-out accuracy.
candidate_050.scope_guard: Do not infer a universal held-out sample count or tolerance from this stellar-stream task or the robotics lifecycle. The proposed gate's causal effect on scientific quality remains unproven.

candidate_049_refinement.name: domain-of-validity and reachable-regime promotion certificate
candidate_049_refinement.new_adjacent_primary_evidence: A 2026 npj Artificial Intelligence Perspective on verification-first autonomous catalysis independently argues that evidence ledgers should record domains of validity and that queries outside prior evidence should be routed to additional computation/experiments rather than confident extrapolation. This is independent design convergence, not a matched efficacy test.
candidate_049_refinement.causal_status: unchanged: mechanism hypothesis; no same-model/tools/budget gate ablation found in this pass

matched_science_repair_search.scope_guard: Verification-first catalysis is a Perspective and adjacent engineering implementations are not substitutes for a matched autonomous-science efficacy experiment.
